text: ConsentFlow is a clinical trial consent rail where the patient stays in control. Instead of a signed PDF locked in a sponsor's filing cabinet, consent becomes a live on-chain state that a participant can grant, scope, and revoke at any time.

The architecture runs on Monad testnet, chain ID ten one four three. A participant's identity is verified through Cleanverse identity, their consent is recorded in the ConsentRegistry contract, and every data contribution mints a receipt token.

This is not a mockup. Two contracts are deployed and verified, backed by fifty five Solidity tests and ten backend integration tests. An independent Prism audit found eleven issues, and all eleven were fixed.
Here is the participant view. To make this demo instant, we embedded a showcase wallet already funded on Monad testnet. One click connects it, no browser extension and no faucet trip required.

The participant picks a study and a purpose. ConsentFlow hashes the study identifier and the purpose string, so the chain stores a verifiable commitment rather than the clinical text itself. That same record can be revoked later by the participant alone.

Now the researcher side. A researcher queues a compensated access request against a specific purpose. The Cleanverse compliance processor is the final gate, and it returns a numeric code that either authorizes the transfer or blocks it.

Every consent grant, revocation, and access decision lands in the audit view. Because the state transitions are on-chain, a regulator or an ethics board can reconstruct exactly who approved what, and when.

The docs page carries the full technical surface: contract addresses, the identity, asset, and compliance endpoints, the test matrix, and the security posture. ConsentFlow fails closed, and it always leaves evidence.
